evidence.exact_text:
Studio is the Handshake-native unified creative suite. It is a kernel-attached creative module in the same architectural position as the atelier module and the Tailor module: a domain subdirectory under `handshake_core` that receives `AppState` by reference, emits `KernelEventType` variants to the EventLedger, operates through the kernel sandbox and `PromotionGate`, persists authority records to Handshake-managed SurrealDB through the official SurrealDB Rust SDK and the kernel's typed authority-store abstraction, and exposes both a native operator UI (egui/wgpu/AccessKit per the canonical native-Rust shell) and a typed model-steerable command/MCP surface.

Studio consists of the following compile units, shared by every creative domain:

1. **`handshake_core::studio`** (`src/studio/`) — the kernel-bound creative module: authority storage, EventLedger emission, CRDT collaborative editing, sandbox dispatch, promotion-gate integration, model-lane binding, and REST/MCP API surface (`src/api/studio.rs`). Per-domain domain logic lives under `src/studio/<domain>/` (e.g. `src/studio/raster/`, `src/studio/vector/`, `src/studio/layout/`).

2. **Independently selectable asset crates** own UI-agnostic domain engines and shared contracts, document graphs, reusable controls, diagnostics and provider adapters. A single engine crate owning all compute is prohibited. Integrated kernel binding consumes typed ports and preserves authority/privacy/promotion/CRDT; GPU/codec dependencies remain selected providers outside handshake_core.

[STU-ARC-001] `handshake_core::studio` is the integrated authority binding, not the owner of compute/domain implementations. It MUST receive the existing `AppState` shared SurrealDB client, model, sandbox, PromotionGate and CRDT infrastructure by reference and register typed Studio API routes in the existing API owner; it MUST NOT initialize duplicate infrastructure. Independently selectable asset leaf crates own domain algorithms, shared document/contracts, reusable controls and provider adapters through typed ports. Their immutable inputs and proposed outputs carry canonical schemas, IDs, units and resource context; only the kernel binding may persist accepted integrated authority through the existing governed lifecycle. Concrete source paths and crate owners MUST be declared in the activated contracts rather than inferred from legacy `src/studio/<domain>/` examples. The existing `StudioEngineError` identifier and typed error semantics, `event_family` constants and canonical event-family values MUST be preserved at the named kernel-binding contract owner. Moving files or splitting providers MUST NOT silently remove or rename these contracts. The activated module/MT map MUST explicitly locate their definitions and API registration consumer, while retaining `storage_glue` responsibility at the binding without forcing legacy directory topology.

Sanitized output MUST exclude disallowed originals, opaque records, thumbnails, history, attachments and metadata from the full reachable payload set; preserving an input file MUST NOT reintroduce removed content. Imports/render/read/retry/export/delivery MUST resolve fresh recipient grants, including linked files and explicitly selected WAL bytes; serialized permission tokens are provenance only. A descriptor list inside a single clause, whether as prose or as a table, is one unit to any derivation tool and therefore loses 12 units of real work.

No other unit yields a microtask. Exactly 6 clauses in this module yield nothing, and they are:

- **Baseline, scope-fence and supersession clauses** — [STU-IO-100], which sits under the bookkeeping heading `0. Baseline, supersession and disposition`. These are discharged when the v02.206 bundle lands, not by a work packet.

Every other clause yields at least one unit. This list is the module's declared non-yielding set and is the authority a derivation tool reconciles against.

**[STU-IO-169] Open items and blocked dependencies.** This module declares no BLOCKED dependency. It does declare a large number of UNKNOWN bounds — every `hard_min` or `hard_max` marked `unknown` in [STU-IO-129], [STU-IO-137] and [STU-IO-143]. An unknown bound is NOT an open item: [STU-IO-103] settles it normatively by requiring the parameter be passed unclamped and the encoder's own error surfaced. Those clauses therefore yield ordinary microtasks. Should a later amendment introduce a genuine open item or a BLOCKED dependency, that clause STILL yields a microtask, and that microtask's FIRST acceptance criterion MUST be resolving the named dependency — reading the named surface, obtaining the named decision, or raising a BLOCKED record with the exact blocker. A declared gap MUST NOT be dropped from the yields index.

## 10.0 SurrealDB Authority Override (v02.205) [SURF-SDB-001]

This override is current product law and takes precedence over all later Calendar, Catalog, Dev Command Center, Notes, Settings, and other product-surface storage text. All durable surface state and EventLedger persistence use Handshake-managed SurrealDB through typed stores. PostgreSQL and SQLite connectivity, dependencies, configuration, credentials, local authority databases, caches, fallbacks, SQL/database importers, reconciliation, fixtures, mocks, tests, and proof paths are forbidden. Existing product features, fields, filters, recovery behavior, offline UX, exports, and operator workflows survive; their storage implementation is translated to `SCHEMAFULL` SurrealQL, authenticated record-user permissions plus ResourceBroker, and SurrealKit rollouts. The external Studio `.lrcat` file-byte decoder is the narrowly bounded exception defined by [STU-OVR-003]; no SQLite engine/database/import-connectivity path is authorized. Fresh SurrealDB/EventLedger cold genesis remains independent of imports.

The later Calendar SQLite DDL, `.hs.catalog.db`, `.handshake/devcc.db`, `devcc.db` migrations, SQL up/down files, and SQLite recovery instructions are non-executable historical semantic inventories. Calendar records, catalog records, DCC projects/sessions/anchors/handoffs/approvals/conversation state, and their EventLedger links are SurrealDB records. ArtifactStore owns materialized artifacts. DuckDB may be retained only as a bounded rebuildable diagnostic/analytics projection with no authority or fallback role. A clean environment initializes SurrealDB and EventLedger genesis without reading or contacting PostgreSQL or SQLite.

Shared development-platform state follows the v02.205 exclusive database law. Handshake-managed SurrealDB is the only durable database authority and persists EventLedger semantics; PostgreSQL and SQLite are forbidden as MCP targets, transactional state, schema tools, caches, fallbacks, SQL/database imports, reconciliation, fixtures, tests, and proof paths. Later PostgreSQL/SQLite/sqlite-utils material is comparative research or non-executable historical inventory only. Implementations use the official SurrealDB Rust SDK, typed store boundaries, `SCHEMAFULL` SurrealQL, authenticated record-user permissions plus ResourceBroker, and SurrealKit rollouts. Any additional database, including DuckDB projections, requires prior explicit Operator approval explaining necessity, preferred database and alternatives; historical comparative inventory is not authorization. The external Studio `.lrcat` file-byte decoder is the narrowly bounded exception defined by [STU-OVR-003]; no SQLite engine/database/import-connectivity path is authorized. Fresh SurrealDB/EventLedger cold genesis remains independent of imports.

[CX-503R] SurrealDB/EventLedger is the exclusive Handshake database authority, including runtime, tests, proof and future self-governance. Do not introduce or preserve SQLite/PostgreSQL connectivity, database-engine import, reconciliation, dual authority, fallback, cache, fixture, compatibility or temporary-adapter paths. Use fresh Handshake-managed SurrealDB state and SurrealKit rollouts. The sole exception is bounded read-only decoding of an Operator-selected external Lightroom `.lrcat` file as untrusted file bytes. The decoder MUST NOT link or invoke a SQL/database engine, expose SQL queries or connectivity, write or repair the catalog, establish a private database/cache/catalog, or treat decoded rows as authority. It emits typed import proposals and provenance/loss receipts; accepted data enters existing CKC and Studio schemas through ResourceBroker, sandbox/validation/promotion and SurrealDB/EventLedger. Every other SQLite/PostgreSQL path remains prohibited. Parser fixtures prove byte decoding only and MUST NOT substitute for production-storage proof. Any proposed additional database requires prior explicit Operator approval with concrete necessity, preferred database and alternatives.
